name: S.O.S. Emergency Food Rations — 3600 Calories
summary: A ready-to-eat ration marketed as 3,600 kcal per packet. The possible two-pack Canadian listing and inconsistent manufacturer calorie arithmetic remain unconfirmed; no 7,200-kcal lot is asserted.
description: A compact ration can provide a reserve when ordinary food is unavailable, but packet count and energy figures must be clear. S.O.S. describes a nine-portion emergency ration without a cooking requirement. The supplied ASIN may represent two packets; that quantity has not been confirmed. The manufacturer nutrition sheet also lists nine 410-kcal servings alongside a 3,600-kcal product name, so this page does not turn either figure into a verified lot total.

pros: The documented ration can be eaten without heating.
Portioned format supports measured short-term distribution once the actual packet label is checked.
cons: Canadian two-pack quantity is not established, so 7,200 kcal for the lot is not verified.
Contains wheat and other potential allergens; a nut-free facility claim does not mean allergen-free food.
useCases: Compare compact ready-to-eat options for an evacuation bag after checking pack quantity and labels.
Plan a rotated reserve with water and a broader range of suitable foods.

confirmed.text: S.O.S. describes a five-year ration and nine servings. Its sheet contains both the 3,600-kcal designation and 410 kcal per serving, which do not reconcile.
The manufacturer FAQ does not offer this ration as gluten-free.

unverifiedClaims: Current Canadian ASIN/model selection, seller, package, lot and delivered-unit labels remain unverified.
safetyNotes: Read the delivered wheat, coconut and soy declarations and full ingredients; this ration is not documented as gluten-free.
A five-year design life is not a promise of five years remaining on an unknown lot. Inspect packaging and dates, and follow storage directions.
Keep potable water available; do not use the illustration as nutrition, ingredient or certification evidence.
publicationBlockers: Independently establish the Canadian listing, delivered variant and safety documentation before full editorial publication.
